visual: Fiery red new leaves ageing coppery then dark glossy green · creamy urn flowers
water: Keep it evenly damp · never standing wet
soilWarning: Ericaceous only · no chalk; wet roots rot
prune: Little needed · take out dead or damaged wood after flowering
toxicity: Harmful if eaten. Harmful to pets if eaten. Wear gloves and protective equipment when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C. Young plants may benefit from winter protection.
resilience: Hardy and long-lived in acid ground · lime and wet roots are the risks
uses: Ericaceous and shrub borders · woodland and courtyard gardens · pots
uncertain: peak: supplied research said "Spring" (the visual says mid spring); converted to Mar-May so the app can parse it, matching the held Pieris 'Forest Flame' card. Not from a source that stated months.

latin: the supplied JSON put the cultivar in cvs and left latin as the bare species. Moved into latin to match the deck's convention, and because the deck's other Pieris is the hybrid 'Forest Flame' with no species name — the two must not be confusable.
aspect: the research named east-, south- and west-facing, so that is used. Derivation from sunNeed 55 alone would have given East / West; a stated facing wins, per tools/fit-incoming.js.
